description: GRBL Robot Arm Warp Transform Calibration Parameters

robot_arm_dimensions.description: Physical dimensions of the robot arm in mm

gear_ratio.description: Motor gear ratio factor (mentioned in mathematician's email)
gear_ratio.note: Factor 0.1 represents motor gearing but was roughly estimated
gear_ratio.explanation: G-code coordinates are translated to motor angles through gearing. G-code thinks it moves X steps in X direction but actually rotates at the axis creating an arc.

calibration_notes.mathematician_email_quote: G-code tror att den flyttar x steg i x-led men den roterar istället vid axeln så att den ritar en cirkelbåge. För att hålla vinkeln inom 180 grader i simuleringen slängde vi helt enkelt in en faktor.
calibration_notes.current_issues: Lines are ridiculously small and positioned far up from original origin coordinates
calibration_notes.calibration_needed: All dimension parameters need adjustment for actual robot arm

test_coordinates.description: Known good coordinates for calibration testing

backup_original_values.description: JBE's original Swedish mathematician values (for reference)

grbl_config_adjustments.description: GRBL configuration constants that need adjustment (from mathematician)
grbl_config_adjustments.note: Förutom att korrigera de mått som finns på maskindelarna i filen vill ni nog se över konstanterna 100 och 101 i GRBL konfig för att justera förhållandet mellan x och y

tuning_suggestions.step2: Check GRBL $100 and $101 settings for X/Y step ratio
tuning_suggestions.step3: Test with simple square coordinates (10,10), (20,20), etc.
tuning_suggestions.step4: Adjust scale_factor if size is wrong
tuning_suggestions.step5: Adjust origin_offset if position is wrong
tuning_suggestions.step6: Fine-tune arm dimensions if shape is distorted
tuning_suggestions.step7: Adjust GRBL $100/$101 if X/Y ratio is incorrect
